note: City of North Platte campground in Cody Park on the North Platte River; large day-use park (lake, mini-zoo, rides, pool). The pads are for small campers or tents; campers report the bigger ones on the river side of the loop, and site 1 is the only pull-through. Quiet generators allowed. The pads sit inside the loop road, with the road and a grass strip between them and the river. --Claude
summary: New city page (northplattene.gov) confirms ~40 pads for small campers or tents, 18-28 ft, no electric, dump, first come, Apr 15-Nov 1, 7 days a month; rate now $20/day (old note $15). Fit is a borderline keep-with-caveat. Riverview stands (pads inside the loop road ~35-50 m from the river). Website moved; pin OK.
flags: FIT (keep with caveat, AWH decides): the city says 'pads for approximately 40 small campers or tents' and 'Pads vary from 18 feet to 28 feet'. Campers: 9/2025 a 22.5-ft motorhome 'fit with no room to spare'; 5/2026 'Most sites are small, would not fit my 30' trailer. There is one pull through site'; 6/2025 'as you loop around and driveway by the rive is where the larger spots are'; 5/2022 a 39-ft motorhome used pull-through site #1. So some pads (the 23-28 ft ones by the river and pull-through #1) fit EKKO, but the page doesn't say how many; it is not 'most under 23' on any count I found. Kept, with the caveat in the note.

WEBSITE: stored https://www.ci.north-platte.ne.us/parks/cody-park/ is dead (404 on 2026-10-15); the city's current page is https://northplattene.gov/548/Parks (Cody Park section, campsites). apply.py doesn't write website.

PHONE: stored 308-535-6706 isn't on the city page; the Parks office number there and on Google is 308-535-6700 (Parks mailing address 1402 N. Jeffers St.). Suggest 308-535-6700. apply.py doesn't write phone.
FEES added (none stored): $20/day from the city page, which is undated. Campers paid $15 (6/2025, 9/2025) and $25 (5/2026), so the posted $20 may itself be out of date; I wrote the operator's figure.

WATERFRONT riverview stands (lead, not a change): on NAIP (220 m frame) the gravel pads are on the inner (south) side of the camping loop road; north of the road is a ~30-50 m strip of grass with picnic tables and scattered trees, then the open braided North Platte (channel 100 m+ wide). The road between the pads and the water rules out riverfront; the river is open and visible. The old note's 'behind the perimeter road and a treeline' overstates the trees (they are scattered, not a continuous line), so I rewrote that sentence.
PIN OK: stored 41.1532,-100.7585 is in the camping loop.
